criteria: ["All seven critical information items must be confirmed with citations for a pass", "Financial figures must carry a period and be consistent across sources", "Key claims need support beyond the issuer's own statements"]
uncertainty: Two critical items are not confirmed: investor-side fees and whether the offering is open. The conversion terms of the two outstanding notes are only partly confirmed. The charter and bylaws, the note instruments, the mouse study report, patent records and any FDA or IRB records are missing. The Form C XML shows $0 long-term debt while the audited balance sheet shows $50,704 of notes. The cash flow statement puts note proceeds under investing. The pack holds only issuer-prepared documents, so nothing is independently corroborated. The result is therefore not a pass. It is unknown, not fail, because the core contract and the audited statements are present.

criteria: ["Pre-revenue company: judge stage-appropriate evidence only, not revenue", "Is there documented, non-issuer-reported evidence that the therapy works or is progressing toward human trials?", "Do the documented team and funding match the plan?", "Are the market and pricing assumptions internally consistent?"]
uncertainty: The only efficacy evidence is one mouse study that the issuer reports, with no sample size, protocol or report in the pack. The issuer says it does not know whether the result will translate to humans. No FDA contact, IND, IRB approval, partner agreement or payer evidence is documented. This is an absence from the pack, not proof that none exists. The team has no documented history of drug or device approval or trial execution. Audited R&D spend was $0 in FY2025 and $26,836 in FY2024. The market section has internal inconsistencies (the 2/3-of-price claim against generic riluzole, 34,000 vs 34,720 patients). The scientific idea could be valid, and nothing in the pack can confirm or refute it. For that reason this is unknown rather than pass or fail.

criteria: ["Is the price tied to any objective measure, and is the implied value reasonable against documented financials?", "Does the security give the investor control, information, anti-dilution or a defined cash path?", "Are dilution sources from existing instruments quantified?", "Are fees and investor-side costs fully disclosed?"]
uncertainty: The price is stated to be arbitrary. Multiplying $1.00 by 75,000,001 founder shares gives about $75M of implied pre-offering equity. That is arithmetic, not a valuation opinion. The founder shares were ratified only in June 2026, with no stated consideration, and the audited balance sheet shows 1 share. Investors give up voting for 10 years through an irrevocable proxy to the founder, who already holds 100% of votes. They get no information rights beyond the legal minimum and no anti-dilution. They hold only a custodian-held securities entitlement. Two notes with undisclosed conversion terms (and a $50,000 add-on on one) sit ahead of the stock. The liquidation preference and dividend terms are in a charter that is not in the pack. Investor-side fees are not found. This result is a fail on contract and price terms only, separate from business quality. I cannot rule out that terms are fairer than they look, for example if the charter has favorable protections.
